questions.question: How should we describe the actual physical shape of cells, even though textbook diagrams often make them look flat?
options: They are completely 2D shapes
They are 3D shapes
They are perfectly flat squares
They are single-layer lines

questions.question: Which of the following lists contains only structures found in typical animal cells?
options: Nucleus, cytoplasm, chloroplasts, cell wall
Cell membrane, nucleus, vacuole, cell wall
Cytoplasm, cell membrane, nucleus, mitochondria
Mitochondria, chloroplasts, large permanent vacuole, nucleus

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a unicellular organism?
options: It is made of a single living cell
It contains exactly two cells working together
It must have millions of cells to survive
It is not made of any cells at all

questions.question: In multicellular organisms, how are jobs divided among the cells?
options: Every single cell performs every job in the organism
Different cells take on different jobs to help the organism function
Cells constantly swap their jobs randomly
Multicellular organisms only use one active cell while others rest

questions.question: What is formed in multicellular organisms when cells of the same type join together to perform a specific job?
options: An organ system
A tissue
A unicellular organism
A chloroplast

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between tissues, organs, and organ systems?
options: Organ systems join together to form a single tissue
Tissues are larger than organ systems and contain organs
An organ is a group of tissues working together, and organs work together in systems
Organs are made of organ systems, which are made of single cells

questions.question: What are the fundamental living building blocks that make up all organisms?
options: Atoms
Minerals
Cells
Tissues

questions.question: Why are cells typically viewed using scientific equipment rather than just looking at a sample with your eyes?
options: Cells are usually too small to see with the unaided eye
Cells only exist when they are under a bright light
Cells are invisible to the human eye under any condition
Cells change color when looked at directly

questions.question: Which scientific instrument is commonly used in classrooms to observe the cells that make up a tissue on a slide?
options: An astronomical telescope
A hand-held magnifying glass only
A light microscope
A barometer

questions.question: To observe cell structures clearly under a light microscope, what two adjustments should you make?
options: Adjust the room lighting and tilt the microscope stand
Change the magnification and adjust the focus
Move the slide to a different table and change the slide cover
Increase the room temperature and shake the microscope

questions.question: Which structures are found in plant cells but are absent in typical animal cells?
options: Cytoplasm and nucleus
Cell membrane and mitochondria
Cell wall, vacuole, and sometimes chloroplasts
Ribosomes and mitochondria

questions.question: What is the main purpose of adding a chemical stain to a cell sample on a microscope slide?
options: To kill any bacteria so the sample is safe to handle
To make it easier to see some parts of the cells
To glue the coverslip permanently to the glass slide
To change the cells into plant cells

questions.question: How should observations made under a light microscope be recorded in a biology practical?
options: In a colorful abstract painting
In a detailed, shaded 3D pencil sketch
In a scientific line drawing
In a written paragraph only with no diagram

questions.question: What is true about specialised cells in animals and plants?
options: They all have the exact same shape and size
They have shapes, sizes, and structures adapted for the jobs they do
They can perform any job in the body at any time
They do not contain a nucleus or cytoplasm

questions.question: Which of the following is a pair of specialised cells?
options: Red blood cells in animals and root hair cells in plants
Skin cells in plants and bone cells in bacteria
Leaf cells in animals and muscle cells in plants
Heart cells in fungi and root hair cells in animals

questions.question: Which group of processes represents the seven life processes that occur in all living organisms?
options: Movement, reproduction, sensitivity, growth, respiration, excretion, nutrition
Breeding, sleeping, thinking, eating, walking, running, growing
Photosynthesis, circulation, digestion, heating, cooling, thinking, moving
Evolution, mutation, adaptation, selection, extinction, growth, reproduction
